title: amr-archetypes: recurring resistance profiles in a bacterial collection, and the diagnostics that decide whether they are real
description:
Python package and command-line tool that clusters one or more binary genotype layers of a bacterial collection (acquired antimicrobial-resistance determinants, virulence loci, capsule or antigen type, plasmid replicons) by similarity-network fusion with order-invariant neighbour selection and consensus clustering, selects a number of groups that may be one, and reports the diagnostics that decide whether the resulting partition means anything: whether the largest group is the trait-absent stratum produced by the empty-union distance convention, whether tied affinities make the answer depend on input row order, whether the fusion collapsed onto a single layer, whether co-inherited loci inflate the feature count, and whether the groups are the lineages relabelled, the last measured as the lineage-attributable share of the partition by an out-of-sample variance decomposition with the partition rebuilt inside every fold.

Post-clustering inference uses multi-split feature splitting with a p-value merging rule valid for exchangeable, arbitrarily dependent p-values, and separates "there is structure" from "that structure is discrete" with a parametric bootstrap from a BIC-selected latent-trait continuum model with adaptive dimension checking and exact finite-bootstrap uncertainty; a phylogenetic convergence test with a Monte Carlo null under a fitted two-state Markov chain, its exact uniform-edge tail reported beside it, serves small cohorts. Every candidate partition, the fusion, the naive concatenation, each single layer and a Bernoulli mixture, is put through the same held-out test, and a measured phenotype, where one is supplied, is the one criterion that is not a function of what was clustered. A five-level machine-readable claim ladder exposes every applicable gate and prevents a partition from being promoted directly to a biological archetype; a failed gate closes the run with a non-zero exit code.

Ships two independently seeded positive controls, a negative and an adversarial control, a Klebsiella pneumoniae case study (1,500 genomes, acquired resistance determinants and virulence loci, sequence type as the lineage, a measured susceptibility panel as the external criterion) and a Streptococcus suis case study (677 isolates, thirteen antimicrobials in two layers, population cluster as the lineage, with full data provenance).

notes: The Klebsiella pneumoniae example data derive from Lam et al. 2021, Nature Communications 12:4188, under CC BY 4.0; the Streptococcus suis example data derive from Hadjirin et al. 2021, BMC Biology 19:191, under CC BY 4.0. Retrieval, epidemiological cut-off derivation, metadata repairs and the population-cluster join are documented and reproducible in the DATA_PROVENANCE.md of each example.
